summary: Swift research program phase 3: one opus agent reads the 5 audits + 7 scouts + frame and writes the prioritised topic map, decides the artifact set, and commissions wave 2 with wave 3 staged
logs: Map: 227 rows · wave2 13 dives in 7 groups · wave3 staged 12 · deferred 38 · owner questions 8 · frame corrections 19

conflicts_resolved: 1 Formatter/linter of record: bundled swift-format with a shipped .swift-format (24 vs 7 repos, 3.4x). SwiftLint optional, custom_rules only (0/42 default hits were defects). An incumbent SwiftFormat is tolerated, never chained (2,795 vs 0 findings). Concurrency 'linting' = compiler diagnostic groups + K-07 grep set.
2 swift format lint exits 0 without --strict (12/12 runs): only the triple format --in-place + lint --strict + git diff --exit-code counts as a gate.

3 Swift Testing vs XCTest: the split is by repo age, not Apple vs community. Swift Testing for unit/integration/CLI e2e/exit tests. XCTest only for XCUITest, measure{} and existing suites. Interop mode: limited vs complete by toolchain/tools >=6.4.

4 Default isolation by target kind: published libraries, SDK, CLIs and servers never set defaultIsolation(MainActor) and must compile under a consumer's default (swift-protobuf compile test); apps and app-internal UI packages may. NNbD/ApproachableConcurrency recommended for new code only with a 6.3+6.4 CI build (flipping it broke 2/6 packages). The 6.4 template is not copied blindly into libraries.

5 Shared state: Mutex<State> by default; an actor only for service state, with a reason comment; @MainActor for UI; global actors niche; NIOLockedValueBox fine inside NIO. @unchecked Sendable / nonisolated(unsafe) only with a visible guard plus an in-code reason, never banned (12/25 avoidable).
6 Typed throws: public API untyped; generic forwarding throws(E); concrete only for closed domains or Embedded (SE-0413; 879 forwarded vs 433 concrete).
7 Package.resolved: repos shipping binaries/apps/images track it and build with --force-resolved-versions; library-only repos gitignore it; a library committing it for its workspace is not a defect.

8 Floors (H1): tools version != language mode. Every target in explicit Swift 6 mode, with per-target .v5 only with a dated reason. Libraries/SDK at the lowest tools version that carries their features, >=6.2 (subprocess 1.0, swift-log 1.16, swift-crypto 5, unsafeFlags). CLIs/servers on the current release. Owner Q1.

9 Warnings-as-errors: CI-flag form on release toolchains, nightlies exempt. .treatAllWarnings only behind an env switch (SwiftPM hides dependency warnings; local path dependencies fail). Groups promoted individually. @diagnose(as: ignored) only with reason:. Provisional, confirmed by W2-4.
10 StrictMemorySafety: CONSIDER by default; SHOULD for packages that wrap C or parse untrusted bytes through pointers (3/40 enable it); never a gate for ordinary code.

11 Macros/swift-syntax: the cost is pin policy, not compile time (prebuilts default on). The fleet does not author macros. Macro packages use a multi-major range + canImport ladder, never exact/branch.

12 Foundation: libraries use #if canImport(FoundationEssentials) when they need no i18n or networking (10.3 vs 55.6 MB static). CLIs may import Foundation. URLSession always behind the canImport(FoundationNetworking) guard.
13 Two rules, not one or many: swift-quality (**/*.swift, 10 depth files) and swift-package (manifest/tool-config names, 2 depth files). No separate concurrency or Apple rule (same glob).

14 Globs: added Package@swift-*.swift (8/15, missed by **/Package.swift) and .spi.yml (31/40, drives the DocC gate). Excluded workflows (never globbed), Dockerfile, pbxproj/xcconfig, .docc, MODULE.bazel, .swiftlint.yaml (not a discovery name, 0/40).

15 Era rows overturned: Android not dropped; FilePath, CommandLine.executablePath, withDeadline and defaultSwiftSettings not in 6.4; @warn is @diagnose; Swift Build is the default; the 6.4 template adds ApproachableConcurrency to every target and sets no language mode; the unsafeFlags block applies only below tools 6.2; upcoming-feature list identical 6.3/6.4; Embedded docs contested; @specialize spelling unresolved.
16 Static binaries: static Linux SDK (musl) for release; --static-swift-stdlib only with --build-system native + issue link (swift-build#1764), since it fails to link under Swift Build.
17 Subprocess: new code uses swift-subprocess from: 1.0.1 (1.0.0 leaks fds; swiftly pins exact 1.0.0). Process only in legacy code, draining both pipes first (hangs at 256 MiB).
18 HTTP: AsyncHTTPClient for credentialed or streamed requests (URLSession on Linux forwards Authorization cross-origin on redirect); URLSession only with a credential-dropping redirect delegate.
19 GCD: no new DispatchQueue for state or main-thread hops, and no DispatchSemaphore.wait in async code. A dedicated queue wrapped in a continuation is OK for blocking C calls.
20 Exit codes: usage errors stay 64 (Windows 160, WASI 1, documented). The Swift SDK maps .signaled(n) to 128+n like Go, not raw like Python (owner Q6).
21 Counting discipline: rules cite the audit counts that exclude tests, fixtures and generated code (@unchecked 564, nonisolated(unsafe) 191). Scout totals (552/862/1131; 2,492) are direction only.
22 Windows (H6): tested in about half the corpus (19-20/40). Rules treat it as first-class (exit 160, rename semantics, no UnixSignals, FilePath Unstable). Local verification depends on owner Q7.

23 DocC gate: generate-documentation --warnings-as-errors with .spi.yml belongs to SW-GATE; doc-comment content stays with code-docs; the code-docs and docs-quality defects are reported to those siblings (M-M-17, M-M-18).
24 H7 MainActor.run: rare in exemplars (23 vs 614 @MainActor); it is an agent habit. The rule targets annotation placement and greps MainActor.run as a tell, not a ban.

artifact_set.rationale: The house rule allows a second rule only for a genuinely different glob. All source concerns (concurrency, errors, CLI, IO, network, security, Apple) bind **/*.swift and route through 10 task depth files. Manifests and tool configs have tool-required names ([map] M1) and get the second rule with gates/release depth. Bazel Swift belongs to the published bazel-quality set as a per-language depth file. Three procedure skills cover the multi-step tasks agents fail at: upgrade/migration, crash/hang diagnosis, release. Bundle swift-essentials = ./swift-quality ./swift-package ./swift-upgrade ./swift-diagnose ./swift-release ./code-docs ./code-docs-cleanup, untagged.
